description: With the implementation of microprocessors, programmable logic devices and DSP chips as controllers in modern systems, this open elective provides a systematic approach to the vital theories required for appreciating the past and present status of control systems.

syllabus.title: Introduction and Signal Processing
syllabus.body: Introduction to digital control systems, overview of the classical approach to analog controller design, advantages of digital control, configuration of the basic digital control scheme, principles of signal conversion, discrete-time signals, sample-and-hold systems, the sampling and hold operations, the sampling theorem, sampled spectra and aliasing, reconstruction of analog signals, choice of sampling rate, principles of discretization, time-domain models for discrete-time systems, transfer function models, stability on the z-plane and the Jury stability criterion.

syllabus.title: Design of Digital Control
syllabus.body: z-plane specifications of control system design, digital compensator design using frequency response plots, digital compensator design using root locus plots, z-plane synthesis.

syllabus.title: Control System Analysis using State Variable Methods
syllabus.body: State variable representation, conversion of state variable models to transfer functions and vice versa, canonical state variable models, eigen values and eigen vectors, concept of controllability and observability.

syllabus.title: Case Studies
syllabus.body: Implementation of digital controllers, tunable PID controllers, digital temperature control systems, digital position control systems, stepping motors and their control, programmable logic controllers.

outcomes: Learn the fundamentals of digital control systems and signal processing.
Design digital controllers and assess their design through constraint specifications.
Model and analyze digital systems in state space.
Learn the applications of digital control for various engineering problems.
textbooks: M. Gopal, Digital Control and State Variable Methods, McGraw Hill Education.
B. C. Kuo, Digital Control Systems, Oxford University Press, New Delhi.
K. Ogata, Modern Control Engineering, Prentice Hall.
referenceBooks: Hemchandra Madhusudan Shertukde, Digital Control Applications Illustrated with MATLAB, CRC Press, 2015.
I. D. Landau and G. Zito, Digital Control Systems: Design, Identification and Implementation, Springer-Verlag.
